title: Weaver (泛微) E-cology / E-office OA — Unauth RCE Chains (BeanShell, SQLi, File Upload)
vuln_pattern: Weaver (泛微) enterprise OA exposes several unauthenticated endpoints with long-standing RCE: a BeanShell servlet that executes Java, SQL-injection endpoints that enable stacked queries/writes, and file-upload actions that drop a JSP webshell.
fingerprint: captcha login on an OA portal
exploit_steps: Fingerprint Weaver from /weaver/ or /wui/ paths, the E-cology/E-office branding, or the OA login.
Try the unauthenticated BeanShell servlet at /weaver/bsh.servlet.BshServlet — POST a `bsh.script` that runs Java (Runtime.exec) for direct command execution.
If BeanShell is patched, try the known unauth SQL-injection endpoints (e.g. WorkflowServiceXml / mobile plugin / api paths) for data read or stacked-query write.
Alternatively use the file-upload getshell path (e.g. KtreeUploadAction / the front-end upload) to drop a JSP webshell, then execute commands.
With code execution, read the flag from the filesystem/DB and exfiltrate. Avoid the captcha-gated interactive login entirely by using these direct endpoints.
key_payloads: unauth SQLi at WorkflowServiceXml / mobile/plugin endpoints
JSP webshell via the Ktree/file-upload action
source: original: Weaver E-cology/E-office public CVE surface (BeanShell/SQLi/upload)
verify_oracle: command execution returns the flag / webshell reads it
pitfalls: do NOT burn time OCR-ing the captcha login — the unauth /weaver endpoints bypass it
